notes: D-006 correction, not oracle parity. Zip entries can carry Unix external file attributes marking an entry as a symlink whose 'content' is the link target string; a naive extractor that only checks the *entry's own path* for traversal (as in zip-slip-relative-traversal-rejected) would still create this symlink on disk pointing anywhere, and any later write through world/link would land at the symlink's target instead of inside the world. MSC 1's shell unzip -o preserves symlink entries verbatim with no inspection at all. Phase 6's extractor must inspect entry type/mode, not just entry path, and refuse an archive containing a symlink entry that resolves outside the target root -- same class of check as fixtures/path-safety's symlink-inside-root-escapes, applied at archive-extraction time instead of live-filesystem-resolution time.
